title: Continuous-section realization of norm-continuous representations
statement: Let $F$ be a normed field and $P$ a topological group. Use the existing all-continuous coefficient ring $C_F$ [def-sfb-norm-continuous-monodromy-data] and internal action modules [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. For a topological $F$-vector space $V$ with continuous addition and scalar multiplication and an $F$-linear representation $\rho$ of $P$, a continuous-section realization is an internal action module $M$ equipped, for every profinite $S$, with additive section identifications $M(S)\cong C(S,V)$, intertwining pointwise $C(S,F)$-scalar multiplication, precomposition restrictions and $g\cdot v(s)=\rho(g(s))v(s)$ for every $g\in C(S,P)$. Every jointly continuous action has a realization. A continuous equivariant linear map determines the unique morphism acting by postcomposition on these sections. Restricting the group action leaves the section realization unchanged. Bundle the same coefficient ring as a commutative ring object, and bundle the existing postcomposition coefficient morphism [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. For its normalized scalar-action restriction [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data], a continuous equivariant semilinear additive map likewise determines the unique action-module morphism with its pointwise section formula. These section descriptions use the existing internal-module/section-module equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. For finite-dimensional scalar-extended representations, use the actual tensor-product module with its finite-dimensional module topology and the tensor-extended action. The fixed subspace is the existing ordinary invariant subspace with its induced residual action. Define its scalar-extended inclusion, restriction of equivariant maps to that subspace, and coefficient insertion from $E\otimes_E V$ to $F\otimes_E V$ by the actual tensor maps. These maps intertwine the actions and their inclusion square commutes.

proof.text: Identify the reconstructed section ring with ULift C(S,F) by the identity on additive sections: Sheaf.μ_comp_map_mul identifies the transported multiplication with pointwise multiplication. Form the presheaf of modules ULift C(S,V), with precomposition as restriction. Continuous maps turn finite coproducts into products and descend uniquely along profinite surjections, which are quotient maps; hence its underlying additive presheaf is a sheaf.

Apply liftedSheafModule and its sectionModuleFunctor counit to the continuous-section module sheaf. On each test object joint continuity gives the pointwise action v(s) ↦ ρ(g(s))v(s), linear over C(S,F). Transport these actions along the linear counit equivalences. The representation laws and precomposition identities give the action monoid homomorphisms and their restriction naturality.

Postcomposition by a continuous equivariant linear map is sectionwise linear and commutes with restrictions. Transport it through the two section equivalences and lift it using full faithfulness of sectionModuleFunctor. Pointwise equivariance gives an action morphism, and evaluation of every section proves uniqueness.

For a semilinear map, use restriction of scalars on the target internal module. Naturality of the lax monoidal tensor comparison identifies its section scalar action with postcomposition by the coefficient ring map. The scalar equation makes sectionwise postcomposition linear. Full faithfulness lifts it; the normalized ScalarAction underlying isomorphism transports it to the prescribed action restriction. ScalarAction.action and pointwise equivariance prove equivariance. Injectivity of the underlying isomorphism and the section formulas prove uniqueness.

The factors (b,1) and (1,l) commute, so the L-action preserves B-fixed vectors. For the fixed inclusion use (b,l)=(1,l)(b,1) and fixedness, first on pure tensors and then by tensor induction. Equivariance sends fixed vectors to fixed vectors. The scalar insertion identities hold on pure tensors by definition and extend by tensor induction or bilinear extensionality.
